title: Button
description: shadcn-style button on the react-aria Button primitive. Callers pass intent props (variant, size), never class names. Primary is a glass pane lit from off-center; hero is the same pane in the dark ramp, the heavy call to action; secondary is the control surface under the primary's own shadow, no lift; discrete is flat text that lifts on hover, copy in bloom, and sinks when pressed; never on a busy background. asChild slots a router Link in place of the button.

anatomy.description: The single root element, a react-aria Button — or, with asChild, the slotted child (a router Link) carrying the same props. Carries data-slot="button", data-variant and data-size for styling hooks and tests.

usage: Use onPress and isDisabled (react-aria semantics), not onClick and disabled.

Variants: primary (default, one per view; the glass pane), secondary (supporting actions; the control surface, --control-fill with --control-hairline, under the pane's shadows, the same --pane-shadow / --pane-shadow-hover / --pane-shadow-pressed values the primary reads from the module's base class, so a primary and a secondary on one row are lit by one lamp; a needle hairline on hover; the pane's pressed shadow when pressed or open. No lift since 2026-10-01, when the extruded recipe became the discrete's hover), hero (né rich, then inverse, renamed 2026-10-01 so the name carries the rule; the primary's pane in the dark ramp, bloom-800 into bloom-900 with needle-50 copy, for a light sheet where the green pane would shout; the heavy call to action, the main character of a page that exists for one thing, a sign-in or a checkout; it stands in for primary, never beside it, nothing else on the page competes with it, and it is used sparsely: one page in many, never one per card), discrete (toolbar and inline triggers; flat at rest, the extruded volume with no fill on hover with bloom-800 copy, takes --control-fill and sinks when pressed or open; chosen 2026-10-01 at /lab/discrete-hover over the wash it replaced. The lift is all it has, so never on a busy background such as a photograph, where the shadows have nothing to cast on: a secondary takes its place there, as on the login). Sizes: mini, small, medium (default). BUTTON_VARIANTS and BUTTON_SIZES export the two axes as lists for a catalogue or a URL schema; the canvas at /components/buttons shows every combination on every surface.

Navigation wears asChild: <Button asChild variant="discrete"><Link to="/dashboard">Discard</Link></Button> keeps anchor semantics under the button's face. Only the slotted element is styled with :hover/:active; react-aria buttons keep data-hovered/data-pressed.

The two panes (primary, hero) are lit from a lamp whose position is the registered custom properties --lamp-x and --lamp-y: the module sets each state's resting position (primary 70%/70%, flipped to 30%/30% when pressed; hero 70%/50%, 70%/70% when hovered or pressed) and a pointer hovering the pane writes its own position inline, one write per frame, so the light follows the hand and glides back when it leaves. Touch never writes; keyboard press keeps the resting flip; prefers-reduced-motion opts out. Nothing to do in a consumer. Prototyped 2026-10-01 at /components/buttons.
State styling keys off react-aria data attributes (data-hovered, data-pressed, data-disabled), so hover stays correct across pointer types.
Field sizes (Input, Textarea, Select) mirror these heights, so a field and a button sit on one row at the same size name.
There is no destructive variant yet; when one is added it MUST use the heartwood ramp, the identity's only red.
An icon inside the button is sized by the button; pass it as a child, do not size it yourself.
